one_liner: Single-header AVX2 C99 lexer with no tables, ~3-6x faster than flex on tokenizing GCC source.
what_it_does: Lexes C-like source (identifiers, strings, comments, common operators) using AVX2 SIMD instructions instead of a flex-generated DFA table. You configure it by defining macros (ALLOWED_TOK2/ALLOWED_TOK3, comment delimiters, ON_TOKEN_CB) before #include "slex.h", then call the lexer over your input buffer; there is no .l grammar file or code-generation step. The callback fires per token with pointers/lengths into the source buffer rather than allocating token objects, so integration means writing C against macros, not compiling a grammar.
how_it_is_fast: Uses AVX2 vector compares to classify characters and find token/line boundaries across chunks in parallel, instead of driving a DFA table one byte at a time like flex. It is table-free: token-class rules are baked in via preprocessor macros and inlined with the callback into a single translation unit, avoiding flex's table lookups and per-transition function-call overhead. The fixed, narrow token set (idents, strings, comments, a small set of 1-3 char operators; no numeric literals) is what makes the branch-light SIMD scan tractable.
when_to_use: Tokenizing large volumes of C-like source (identifiers, string/char literals, // and /* */ comments, common short operators) where flex's DFA walk is the bottleneck
x86-64 build targets with AVX2 available and a willingness to compile with -march=native or explicit AVX2 flags
Prototyping a custom lexer where hand-writing token-class macros is acceptable instead of authoring a flex grammar
Workloads that don't need numeric-literal lexing, or where you're willing to add that yourself
Small, embeddable single-header C99 codebases that want to avoid a flex/bison toolchain dependency
when_not_to_use: Need numeric literal (int/float) tokenization out of the box -- not implemented
Targeting non-x86 or pre-AVX2 hardware -- no scalar or NEON fallback path in the header
Need an actively maintained project -- last commit 2021-09-24, author describes it as a 'proof-of-concept', 19 stars
Want flex-style declarative grammar files or code generation rather than macro-configured C source
Need the published 34ms/231ms benchmark to be independently reproducible -- the flex reference binaries and their build flags live outside this repo

integration.dependencies: none beyond libc (string.h, stddef.h, stdint.h); immintrin.h when __AVX2__ is defined
integration.min_toolchain: C99 (Makefile uses --std=gnu99); GCC/Clang path exercised, MSVC intrinsics branches present but build recipe targets gcc; needs -march=native or equivalent AVX2 flag
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 required; no aarch64/NEON port documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces flex's role as a lexer but requires hand-integrating macros and a callback before including the header, not a .l-file-equivalent drop-in

gotchas: Must define ALLOWED_TOK2/ALLOWED_TOK3, comment start/end tokens, and ON_TOKEN_CB before #include "slex.h" -- the header ships no default token set
ON_TOKEN_CB must be a static inline function defined in the same translation unit; the header's own comments say a function-pointer callback is slower
Does not lex numeric literals -- README lists this as 'on the way' but it's not in the shipped code as of the last commit
Requires AVX2 (__AVX2__); nothing in the header falls back to a scalar path if it's unavailable
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick simd-lexing only when you want a tiny, dependency-free single-header C lexer to vendor and hand-tune via macros for a narrow token set; Accelerated-Zig-Parser and Gigatoken report larger speedups with more reproducible harnesses, and CrossDB's hand-written lexer/parser is actively maintained, so any of those is a better default if you need a supported project rather than an abandoned proof-of-concept.
verified_claims_summary: On a single concatenated file of GCC source (identifiers/strings/comments only, no numeric literals) on a Skylake 2.40GHz i5 laptop, the README's gcc --std=gnu99 -O3 -march=native build of simd-lex ran in 34ms versus flex at 231ms (default), 102ms (--fast) and 106ms (--full) -- roughly 6.8x and ~3x faster respectively; timings come from single shell `time` runs (including process startup/I/O) and the flex reference binaries plus their build flags are not included in the repo.
status_note: Abandoned since its last commit on 2021-09-24 -- the author calls it a proof-of-concept -- but it's Zlib-licensed and small enough (one header) to vendor and maintain yourself.
